section_summary.extract_value: This discussion summarizes a single study (N=253 women from the general population) that tested a mediated model where social safeness predicts disordered eating via body appreciation (BAS-2) and inflexible eating rules, controlling for BMI. The authors note limits (cross-sectional design, exclusive female community sample, self-report measures) and suggest future research including longitudinal designs and more diverse samples.

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion reports results from a single cross-sectional study (N=253) of women from the general population showing that social safeness is positively associated with body appreciation (BAS-2) and negatively associated with inflexible eating rules and disordered eating; path analysis indicated these two mechanisms mediate the association between social safeness and eating psychopathology (model explained R2 = 0.58 for EDE-Q). Limitations noted include the cross-sectional design, exclusive use of self-report measures, and an all-female general population sample, limiting causal inference and generalizability.

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion reports a single cross-sectional study testing a path model in a sample of women from the general population (N=253) examining social safeness, body appreciation (BAS-2), inflexible eating rules (IEQ), BMI, and disordered eating (EDE-Q). Fig. 1 displays the final path model showing BAS-2 and IEQ as mediators between social safeness and disordered eating while controlling for BMI; limitations include cross-sectional design, female-only sample, and self-report measures.
